title: Test-Ready Basics (JLPT N5)
description: Essential grammar particles (wa, ga, o, ni, de) and foundational polite copula and verb conjugations.
reviewedBy: Kazi Sakib (Founding Mentor, University of Tokyo)

items.prompt: Which particle marks the overarching topic of a sentence (written as 'ha' but pronounced 'wa')?
items.explanation: The topic marker particle is written as は (ha) but pronounced 'wa' when functioning as a particle.

items.prompt: Which particle marks the direct object of an action verb (e.g. 'hon ___ yomu')?
items.explanation: The direct object marker particle is を (o/wo).

items.prompt: Which particle indicates the location where an action takes place (e.g. 'toshokan ___ benkyou suru')?
items.explanation: で (de) indicates location of action ('at/in'), instrument/means ('by train'), or materials.

items.prompt: What is the polite past tense of 'desu' (is/are)?
items.explanation: The polite past tense of です (desu) is でした (deshita).

items.prompt: Which particle marks a specific time point or destination target (e.g. '7-ji ___ okiru')?
items.explanation: に (ni) marks specific time points ('at 7:00'), destinations ('go to Japan'), and indirect objects.
